title: A Bucket of Blood

evidence.note: Published in 1959, so public domain status would depend on a missing copyright notice or a missing renewal in the 1986-1988 window. I found no Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal entry and no document proving a renewal is absent. A web search for the title and Alta Vista Productions returned no renewal record, but a failed search does not prove absence. The Internet Archive items carry a Public Domain Mark 1.0 label on one upload and a CC0 licence URL on the other. Those are the uploaders' claims, not evidence.

Fred Katz is credited as composer. A sound film's recorded track normally shares the film's status, so the score likely follows the print, but the print status is itself unconfirmed. I found no separate music registration or renewal record.

Screenplay credited to Charles B. Griffith. I did not confirm whether it was an original work or whether a separate screenplay registration exists. The 1995 television remake and the later stage musicals are separate derivative works.

Wikipedia reports an MGM Home Entertainment DVD release in 2000 with supplementary materials. I did not find a documented restoration. Any added material on a commercial disc could carry its own protection. The Internet Archive scan is described as an HD scan.

editorial:
A Bucket of Blood is Roger Corman's 1959 black comedy about Walter Paisley, a talentless busboy at a bohemian café who becomes an acclaimed sculptor after covering his landlady's dead cat in plaster, then keeps producing sculptures by increasingly sinister means. Dick Miller plays the lead, Charles B. Griffith wrote the screenplay, Fred Katz composed the score, and American International Pictures distributed it. Internet Archive describes it as shot quickly on leftover sets that were reused for The Little Shop of Horrors.

The rights trap is that the copyright status is unconfirmed. The film was published in 1959, so a renewal was due in 1986 to 1988. I found neither a renewal record nor a record proving none exists. The Internet Archive labels and Wikipedia's public-domain listing are not primary sources. Before commercial reuse, search the Copyright Office public records and the CCE renewal volumes yourself. The 1995 TV remake and the stage musicals are separate works with their own rights, and a commercial DVD such as MGM's 2000 release may add protected material.
faq: Is A Bucket of Blood in the public domain?

Unconfirmed. The Internet Archive labels its copies Public Domain Mark or CC0 and Wikipedia lists the film as public domain. I found no primary record showing a missing notice or a missing renewal. Check the Copyright Office public records and the CCE renewal volumes for 1986-1988 before relying on it.
Can I use the Internet Archive copy in a commercial project?

Not safely until the renewal check is done. The upload's public-domain label is the uploader's claim. The 1995 remake and the stage adaptations are separate copyrighted works and are not covered by the original film's status.
